knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The practice note requires a building permit for attached decks irrespective of size [VBA-BP01], so the size is not a reason to skip the check.
A wrong boundary line creates a dispute and may breach the owner's right to build, so the line is confirmed from the owner's documents first.
The NSW exempt limit for a masonry side or rear fence is 1.2 metres [NSW-FENCE], so 1.5 metres is outside the exempt rule and the planning route must be checked.

practicalCriteria: Produces a scope record for a sample job showing the owner's written authority, the property address and the boundary source, checked by the assessor against a checklist.

Records the permit, planning and licence positions for a sample Victorian attached deck and a sample New South Wales fence, each with the source name and page date, and leaves out any item where no source was checked.
Writes a referral note for a sample boundary dispute, and shows that setting out is held until the reply is filed.
passRule: Assessor review of the scope record, the permit and licence check records and the referral note for the sample jobs, with all three practical criteria met. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Scope record with owner's written authority and boundary source
Permit, planning and licence check record with source name and page date
Referral note with the reply on file
stopWorkCriteria: Setting out or digging starts before the boundary is confirmed from documents
The owner's authority is not written or cannot be confirmed
A boundary dispute is open and the line is still being set out
The permit or planning position is unknown and no referral has been made
